the 6-O-(1)F-fluoromethylated derivatives of diprenorphine (antagonist), buprenorphing (partial agonist), and phenethyl-orvinols (full agonist) were prepared and evaluated as functional analogues of the carbon-11 labeled compounds.

the 6-O-(19)F-fluoromethylated diprenorphine is the most suitable radiotracer for in vivo mu-opioid receptor (MOR) imaging in terms of pharmacokinetic properties, and that the 6-0-(18)Ffluoroethylated buprenorphines, in particular, [(18) F]FPEO, may be the best candidates to image MORs in humans with PET.

the three 6-[(18)F]F-alkyl-derivatives are suitable candidates for the development of novel PET ligands for imaging the mu opioid receptor in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
[(18)F]-FDPN and [(18) F]-FPEO are suitable as antagonists and agonist, respectively, and [(18)]F-FPEO is a promising radioligand for imaging of μ-opioid receptors in the brain.

6-O-desmethylation of the 6-O-(3H)-methylated orvinols is a useful approach for preparing 6-O-(fluoroalkyl)-derivatives with similar properties to the carbon-11 labeled analogues, and that [(18)F]-fluoroethylated orvinol derivatives are promising candidates as radiotracers for mapping opioid receptors in vivo with PET.
the [(18)F]-fluoroethylated orvinols have been shown to be useful tools for in vivo studies of mu opioid receptor pharmacology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

[(18)F]-fluoroethylated derivatives can be used as a general approach to produce a wide range of 6-O-[18F]fluoroethylester derivatives of structurally diverse opioids with different intrinsic activities.
6-O-[18]F-fluoro-ethylated derivatives of orvinol analogues can be synthesized and used as PET radiotracers to study mu opioid receptor occupancy and function in vivo.

the 6-O-desmethylation of the orvinols does not significantly change the intrinsic activity of the orvinol derivatives and that the 6-alkylation of the phenethyl-orvinols is a suitable route to produce 6-alkylated derivatives with similar pharmacological profiles to the native orvinols.
